Subject: Re: Kickoff: cost/perf tuning items before P0 launch

Samantha —

Love the clarity on the timeline. Quick proposed plan in bullets; I attached an editable mutual_action_plan.xlsx for your PM and procurement teams.

- Immediate defaults (suggested, can canary): batching target = 8 requests per batch, burst up to 32 when latency < 150ms; cache prefix TTL = 30m for user-level session queries, KV hot-key TTL = 6h for repeated context sets.
- Quantization: start with int8 dynamic for inference (good latency/cost balance), have an int4-safe profile as backup for low-cost exploratory runs (expect ~15-25% quality delta, will provide eval examples).
- Routing policy (first 2 weeks): latency-first for prod routes during internal tests (route to dedicated pool in us-west), with a cost-fallback policy to int8-hosted variant if dedicated capacity is saturated.
- Canary & rollout: 5% canary for 48 hours on full traffic profile, then 25%/50%/100% increments over a week if metrics hold.
- Procurement/security: attached SOC2 extract and we will enable KMS + audit logs for your compliance team on day 1.

Next steps: Marissa will own the mutual action plan edits and Priya will propose the quant-profile CSV with exact param settings. Can we sync Wed 11/03 11am PT for a quick handoff?

Avery
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Adding a bit more structure to the shared plan (see attached):

- Mutual Action Plan (sheet 1): owner, due date, acceptance criteria. I've added Procurement sign-off row and a 'security evidence' checklist for SOC2 snippets and KMS envelope configs.
- Implementation checkpoints (sheet 2): 1) Config staging in your VPC sandbox (day 1-2); 2) Canary traffic run (day 3); 3) Quant regression check using your eval prompt set (day 4); 4) Full ramp (day 7).
- Risk mitigations: automatic fallback to Hosted int8 variant if latency SLOs degrade by >20% for >5 minutes; also recommend an early 2-hour maintenance window during ramp for quick rollback.

Priya — can you attach the quant_profiles_v1.csv in this thread with the exact kernel/config keys (eg: quant_type=int8_dynamic, per_channel=true, weight_bits=8, kv_cache_prefetch=true)? Sam/Carlos — if you can share a short eval prompt set (5-10 examples) we will run a quick quality delta check between float16/int8/int4-safe.

Marissa

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@fidelisai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Quant profiles and quick eval plan

Hi team —

Attached is quant_profiles_v1.csv (short version in body below). High-level guidance:
- Profile A (default): int8_dynamic, per_channel=true, weight_bits=8, activation_quant=false — balanced latency/cost, good for production.
- Profile B (cost-first): int4_safe, per_channel=false, weight_bits=4, activation_quant=true — use only for non-critical exploratory routing and only when workload is mostly short prompts (<512 tokens).
- Profile C (quality): float16 baseline for critical flows (customer-visible summarization).

Quick eval plan: we will run a 200-sample subset of your drive eval prompts across the three profiles and produce PPL/ROUGE-ish quality deltas and 95p latency comparisons. Expected results communicated in 48 hours after you confirm sample set.

Short excerpt from quant_profiles_v1.csv:
profile_id,quant_type,per_channel,weight_bits,activation_quant,use_case
A,int8_dynamic,true,8,false,prod-balanced
B,int4_safe,false,4,true,explore-cost
C,float16,false,16,false,critical-quality

Priya
Applied ML — Redwood Inference
